anthropic/claude-opus-5-5.feedback: Only `create` moved, and it moved on the title transport. Before put the landed subject in the command as a single-quoted literal, so the title text sat inside shell source. After writes it to a file and passes it as one quoted `"$LANDED_SUBJECT"` argument set inside the same call, so neither title nor body text is in the command. The rest was already in place in both outputs: the unchanged five-option menu with no Integration question, the verbatim Integration block once after Test Plan with the literal EOF and End of receipt lines, the minted path as one `--body-file` argument, the `cd` into `/work/import queue`, and the block-only replacement in the draft body that preserves the surrounding text and spacing. One fragility remains: After invents a sibling `pr-body.B72pL3.title` path that the mint never printed, and the output only asserts that the title was written there. To make this robust, the wording should say where the title data file comes from (its own mint, or an explicitly derived sibling of the minted body path) and that the file writer writes it as data in the earlier call. Keep the existing requirements that the create call uses the printed body path verbatim, sets any variable inside the same call, and runs in the observed worktree.

github-copilot/gpt-6.1-sol.feedback: The offer and the updated draft body are identical in Before and After: the five-option menu is in order with no Integration question, and the draft body replaces only the stale Integration block while keeping the lead line's double spacing and the Notes section. So `update` already held in Before and did not move as expected. The only fact that moved is `create`, and it moved on the title transport alone. Both outputs carry the Integration section verbatim once after Test Plan (including the indented instruction and the literal EOF and End of receipt lines), claim nothing was checked, and pass the minted path `/work/import queue/.git/gauntlet/tmp/pr-body.B72pL3` as one quoted `--body-file` argument from a `cd` into the worktree. Before fails because it inlines the subject as a single-quoted string in the command, which puts title text in shell source. After holds because it reads the subject from a companion `.title` file into a variable set and expanded as `"$LANDED_SUBJECT"` within the same call, so the backticks and `$(import)` arrive as one literal argument with no reliance on earlier shell state. To keep this robust, state explicitly in the wording that the title is written as data by the file writer to a path derived from the minted body path, and is read inside the create call itself. Otherwise a reader may question whether the `.title` path counts as the same minted scratch path, or the output may drift back to an inline quoted title. Keep the wording that makes the offer independent of the Integration entries and that reconciles only the Integration block on an existing PR, since those are what hold `offer` and `update`.
